title: Schedules
description: The Swift app's schedule routes, field for field (its docs/schedules.md and RemoteServer.swift): GET and POST /v1/orchestrator/schedules, GET, PATCH and DELETE /v1/orchestrator/schedules/:id, POST /v1/orchestrator/schedules/:id/run. The stored schedule is the Swift app's schedule file; see ScheduleFile. The generator has no union type, so `days` is typed only in its array spelling — the routes also accept and return the string `daily` there.

at.description: When the run's task was created, Unix seconds.

state.description: The task's state: queued, spawning, briefed, success, failure, timeout, cancelled or spawn_failed.

ScheduleRow.description: One row of the list, in one of two shapes. A valid schedule carries id, title and enabled, and whichever of the rest apply. A schedule this daemon cannot parse carries only file, state (`invalid`), error and error_kind (`schema`, `project_unavailable` or `unreadable_json`) — it is listed rather than hidden, because a row that vanishes is a row nobody can fix. No task-template field is listed but project_dir.

fired_at.description: A schedule that runs once, and has: when its session opened. Such a schedule never fires again.

last_missed_at.description: The most recent occurrence that expired outside its catch-up window.

next_fire.description: The next local fire, Unix seconds. Absent for a schedule that will not fire again.

once.description: Present and true for a schedule that runs once (`when.on`).

state.description: `invalid` on a row that could not be parsed; absent otherwise.

ScheduleWhen.description: `when` in the file's own spelling: `at` (HH:MM, local time) and exactly one of `days` (`daily`, or weekday names sun…sat) or `on` (YYYY-MM-DD, a schedule that runs once).

ScheduleRun.description: One task a schedule made, newest first in the detail. `summary` is what the task wrote when it finished.

ScheduleRecord.description: GET /v1/orchestrator/schedules/:id: one schedule in full — the template and the retained runs the list leaves out. `webhook_binding_availability` is `active` (with `webhook_hook_id`), `unbound`, or `binding_store_unavailable`.

ScheduleTask.description: The task template, as the file carries it. The fields a request may never name — project_dir, claims and the rest — are set in the file and carried across every save. permission_mode is the form's own field (ScheduleRequest).

ScheduleRequest.description: The body POST /v1/orchestrator/schedules and PATCH /v1/orchestrator/schedules/:id take — the form's fields, flattened. `place_id` is an id from GET /v1/places, never a path. Exactly one of `days` and `on`; `days` is not defaulted. schedule_id, created_at, when_changed_at, fired_at and project_dir are the machine's and are refused as unknown fields. Writes need an Idempotency-Key and either a device that may send or, for a schedule that runs once, this machine's orchestrator token. A session carrying a person's recent instruction may write a repeating schedule by sending both `session_id` and `via.run`; the run must have been issued for a message to that conversation. Those proof fields are audit evidence and are not stored in the schedule.

model.description: No key leaves the model alone; an empty string takes it off.

permission_mode.description: ask, edits or full; an empty string takes it off (this machine's default); no key keeps what the file says. Only a person's device sets or changes it: this machine's orchestrator token, and a session carrying a person's message, are refused with permission_needs_person unless the value is what the file already says.

session_id.description: The conversation the person's message was sent to. Required with via for a session-authorized repeating write.

ScheduleTemplate.description: Task-template fields the form has no control for, which a create may carry — what a save already carries from the stored file, so a schedule moved from another machine arrives as it was. Accepted on POST only; a PATCH that names it is refused, because a save carries the stored fields itself. The file's parser reads each value, as it reads a stored file. `graph` is accepted too, as a stored file holds it (the generator has no type for it). `permission_mode` is refused by name (`template_permission_mode`): it is sent as the form's own field, where who may set it is checked. Any other key is refused by name. `reasoning_effort` is kept only when the assistant is codex, as a save keeps it.

ScheduleUserAuthorization.description: The recent run issued when the person sent this session the instruction. Required with session_id for a session-authorized repeating write.

ScheduleSaved.description: A made or saved schedule. `dispatch_enabled` rides beside a made one only: writing a schedule is not dispatching, and with task dispatch switched off nothing runs it.
